newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks soar 1.41 pct to 22-month high close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks soar 1.41 pct to 22-month high close.

text.p: Taiwan's financial sector stole the limelight from electronics to post sharp gains on Monday, driving the market to yet another 22-month high amid what one broker called "extreme bullishness".
The weighted index ended up 96.71 points or 1.41 percent at 6,938.87, the highest since January 1, 1995.
The bull run turnover was a sizzling T$115.29 billion, the largest single-day volume since June 14.
The heavily weighted financial shares surged 2.44 percent to lead the gains, seizing on high expectations for United World Chinese Commercial Bank's November 29 listing, brokers said.

Several shares linked to United World -- those which should profit by the new listing because of their big shareholdings in the bank -- rose to boost the already bullish sentiment, said Amy Huang, an analyst at Nomura Securities.
These included Chiao Tung Bank and Farmers Bank, which rose the daily seven percent limit to T$87.5 and T$60, respectively.
Brokers noted persistent buying momentum despite the fact that -- even before Monday's session -- the index had gained nearly 300 points in November.
The index set 22-month highs every day last week except Thursday, with red-hot electronics shares leading the pace.
As the focus shifted to financials, new money flowed in.
"Many individual investors withdrew their time deposits from banks and jumped in, fearing they might not be able to catch this bullet train," Nomura's Huang said after Monday's close.
Allen Huang, a National Securities manager, made a similar assessment: "The large turnover indicates an aggressive attitude right now, that the market is basking in extreme bullishness."

The bull run has been fuelled by a sound outlook for 1997, especially for electronics and other fundamentals-based shares, and by early year-end window dressing from local securities investment trust funds, brokers said.

Major-capital shares also attracted buying as foreign securities houses including Baring and BZW have issued warrants on Taiwan's blue chips, brokers said. Acer surged T$3 to T$54 and China Petrochemical rose T$2.1 to T$38.1.
Glass, rubber, hotel and transportation shares were strong.
Some electronics shares fell victim to profit-taking, with chipmaker First International falling T$3 to T$56.

Brokers said the market had largely ignored a strategically important meeting on Sunday between U.S. President Bill Clinton and China's President Jiang Zemin in the Philippines, even though better U.S.-China ties are sure to affect Taiwan.
With resistance at 6,900 already breached with seemingly little effort, analysts sadi the index could test 7,000 as early as Tuesday.
"Around 7,100 points, we will see stronger technical resistance, and after this recent rally, we may see bigger downward corrections soon," Nomura's Huang said.
